clue.text: He is officer getting drunk — what's the drink?

indicators.note: someone getting drunk is all over the place, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: An officer has had one too many, and someone asks what he has been drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' reads as the officer's state, but together with 'getting' it signals the anagram of HE IS OFFICER.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot whiskey with coffee, sugar and cream on top is a well-known after-dinner drink.

clue.text: Grasses about to meet newspaper folk?

parts.note: re is Latin-derived shorthand for about or concerning
eds is short for editors, the people who run newspapers

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether grasses are about to meet some journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall marsh and waterside plants of the grass family are called by this name.

clue.text: Strike is upsetting local community — 500 involved

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the word is upside down, so it reads from bottom to top
something involved is caught up inside, so the 500 goes inside the community

parts.note: a town is a local community
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A strike disrupts a local community, with 500 people taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' is the definition, a protest where workers stay seated; 'upsetting' looks like the strike's effect but reverses IS, and 'involved' puts D inside TOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest in which workers occupy their workplace and refuse to work is a kind of industrial strike.

clue.text: Two firms operating in a secure environment

parts.note: CO, short for company, is a firm; two of them give it twice
a machine that is operating is on

explanation.surface: Two companies are working within a safe setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A protective casing spun by a larva, and figuratively any sheltered, safe surrounding.

clue.text: Enjoyment before almost everyone becomes gloomy

parts.note: fun is enjoyment
ere is a poetic word for before

indicators.note: almost says the last letter of the word for everyone is dropped

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Having fun before nearly everybody turns depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' looks like it orders the pieces, but it is the poetic word ERE; 'almost' drops the last letter of ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Suited to a burial, so sombre and mournful in mood.

clue.text: Not all hear a cheer — a problem for some listeners

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Not everybody hears the crowd's cheer, which some listeners find a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain in the ear is a complaint for anyone using their ears, playfully called listeners.

clue.text: More helpful, having reformed strange facilities for youngsters

parts.note: kinder means more helpful or considerate

indicators.note: reformed means given a new shape, so the letters of strange are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone became more helpful after changing their odd ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having reformed' looks like a person's change of character; 'reformed' rearranges STRANGE into GARTENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursery schools for young children before formal schooling are facilities aimed at the very young.

clue.text: Struggle as a swimmer in the sea

definitions.meaning: to struggle or thrash about clumsily
a flatfish found in the sea

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to struggle helplessly and a kind of flat sea fish.

clue.text: Ornamental material revealed by girl's mum

parts.note: mum is mother
a girl named Pearl, so the possessive reads of Pearl

explanation.surface: An ornamental fabric is shown off by a girl's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'girl's mum' as the mother of a girl called Pearl.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre, the iridescent lining of oyster shells, is used for decorative inlays and buttons.

clue.text: Home pet, terribly clumsy

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so the letters of pet are mixed up

explanation.surface: The family pet at home is dreadfully awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking skill or awkward in handling things is a synonym.

clue.text: Singer in incomplete command, needing to hold key

indicators.note: needing to hold says the shortened word contains the key
incomplete says the word for command loses its last letter

parts.note: control is command
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A singer is not fully in charge and has to keep to a musical key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks musical but is the computer key ALT; 'incomplete' trims CONTROL to CONTRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A female vocalist with the lowest voice range is an example of a singer.

clue.text: Daughter is taking time — in that there is no shame

indicators.note: the phrase says the word for time has the following word sitting inside it

parts.note: an hour is a period of time

explanation.surface: A daughter takes her time, and there is no disgrace in that.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'no shame' sounds like the verdict, but only 'shame' defines; 'in that there is' puts the clue's own NO inside HOUR, and 'taking' simply joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of respect or reputation, disgrace, is a close synonym.

clue.text: A hundred hurry — there's this danger with stampede

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
rush means hurry

explanation.surface: A hundred people rush at once, and a stampede brings this danger.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense mass of people pressed together is the hazard a stampede brings.

clue.text: Hurry to engage trendy French dramatist

indicators.note: to engage something is to hold it, so the word for hurry contains the trendy word

parts.note: race means hurry
in means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: Someone rushes to sign up a fashionable French playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Racine wrote seventeenth-century French tragedies such as Phèdre.

clue.text: Female gang to afflict Midlands city

parts.note: a coven is a group of witches, typically women
to try is to afflict or put to the test

explanation.surface: A gang of women sets out to trouble a city in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in the West Midlands of England, famous for its cathedral.

clue.text: A learner with aim to get into vehicle for a series of dates

indicators.note: to get into says the pieces go inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
L is the learner driver's plate
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A learner driver aims to climb into a car for a run of appointments.
explanation.definitionFit: A table listing the days of the year in order is a run of dates.

clue.text: What sounds like excellent university in Scotland

indicators.note: the phrase says the answer is a word said the same way as one meaning excellent

parts.note: sterling means excellent or of great worth

explanation.surface: Someone asks which Scottish university sounds first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A university founded in 1967 in the Scottish town of the same name.

clue.text: Recommend veto, a cad needing to be dealt with

indicators.note: as with cards that are dealt out, the letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone urges a veto because a rogue must be handled.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak in favour of something or urge it publicly is to recommend it.

clue.text: Dog outside hospital department, a beast seemingly half human

indicators.note: outside says the dog word wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A dog waits outside a hospital ward, looking like a creature only half human.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this creature has a man's upper body on a horse's frame.

clue.text: Important Arab severe, no end, with condition laid down

indicators.note: no end says the word for severe loses its final letter

parts.note: sharp means severe, as of a frost
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A stern Arab leader lays down terms without end.
explanation.definitionFit: A title for a descendant of the Prophet, used of Arab nobles or leaders.

clue.text: Difficult to deal with that topless 'nutcase'

parts.note: hard means difficult

indicators.note: in a down clue, topless removes the first letter of that

explanation.surface: That headless madman is hard to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nutcase' reads as a lunatic, but nut is slang for head, so it is a case for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Protective headgear is a case for the nut, slang for the head.

clue.text: Dad and I heard comic sailor

parts.note: pop is an informal word for dad

indicators.note: heard says the word I is used for how it is said, not how it is spelt

parts.note: the pronoun I is said exactly like eye, the organ of sight

explanation.surface: Father and I listened to a funny seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinach-eating cartoon sailor is a famous comic-strip character.

clue.text: No fabric for putting around a bit of wood?

indicators.note: putting around turns the pieces round so they read backwards

parts.note: net is a fine mesh fabric

explanation.surface: Someone asks what to wrap round a piece of timber, when there is no cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A projecting piece shaped on the end of timber to fit a mortise joint.

clue.text: Big river or little one gone arid unfortunately

parts.note: a little river: R is the short form of river

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A great river, or a small one, has sadly dried up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little one' means a small river, the abbreviation R; 'unfortunately' rearranges GONE ARID.
explanation.definitionFit: A major North American river forming part of the US-Mexico border.

clue.text: Soldier ultimately quits on promotion? Under no circumstances!

indicators.note: in a down clue, promotion raises the letters so they read upwards
ultimately takes the last letter of soldier

parts.note: being quits means being even, owing nothing

explanation.surface: A soldier finally leaves after promotion, asking whether it should never happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promotion' looks like military rank, but reverses R + EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: At no time or not at all, an emphatic refusal.

clue.text: King Baddy in simplistic story

indicators.note: in says the king and the baddy sit inside the simplistic word

parts.note: naive means simple or simplistic
R stands for rex, Latin for king
a rat is a villain or betrayer

explanation.surface: A king and a villain feature in a simple tale.
explanation.definitionFit: An account of connected events is a tale or story.

clue.text: Linger as husband left after others have gone?

parts.note: something left over remains after the rest have gone

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to linger as the husband who stays behind after everyone leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang about or stay close by in one place is to linger.

clue.text: Hemmed in by youngsters, great man falls apart, broken

indicators.note: hemmed in by says the anagram sits inside the word for youngsters

parts.note: fry are young fish, hence youngsters

indicators.note: falls apart means breaks into pieces, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Surrounded by children, a great man collapses in pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Fry, young fish, stand in for youngsters; 'falls apart' rearranges GREAT MAN to RAGMENTA, and 'Hemmed in by' sets that inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Existing only in bits or incomplete pieces, so broken up.
